correctness.rationale: Exact four-by-four determinant, independent squared-eigenvalue positivity test, discriminant factorization, and strict normalized-width monotonicity produce the theorem without sampling. At exceptional boundaries the irreducible tridiagonal eigenvector recursion proves a one-dimensional eigenspace. Verified exact symbolic identities and sampled direct complex-matrix eigenvalues agree; no finite sweep is treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Published work established qualitative PT restoration and four-mode coupling dependence, but no checked material establishes the conjunction of this explicit opposite-end gain/loss model, the iff ratio 2<t<1+sqrt(2), and the sharp normalized recovered-width supremum with nonattainment and cusp law. The accessible primary 2014 original uses oscillatory on-site gain/loss profiles, while the 2015 four-mode preview distributes gain over two sites and loss over two other sites. Historical completeness is not claimed, and inaccessible original material is a stated risk.
residual_risks: The full original 2015 Rivolta–Maes manuscript was inaccessible through available public/OA and authorized institutional paths; only its first-page scientific material and abstract were checked.
Equivalent end-gain four-site formulas or fixed-budget optimizations may exist in non-indexed or differently worded older coupled-mode literature.
The sum-of-link magnitudes is a mathematical design constraint; practical fabrication may impose different constraints.

value.rationale: For PT-symmetric waveguide designs a gain interval with entirely real spectra is useful only if it has nonzero calibration margin. The theorem gives an optimal universal margin bound strictly under 7% of total couplings, no attaining design, and an explicit first-order tradeoff against introducing a broken phase. The complete sharp constrained design classification and endpoint exceptional-point structure are nontrivial natural invariants, distinct from just detecting an exceptional point.
